questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: You can go through the intersection safely if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go through the intersection safely if the way is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you may proceed. Always check that the intersection is clear and yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in it.

questions.question: It is illegal to:

options.text: Pass in a marked no passing zone.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass in no passing zones or over railroad crossings. You also cannot pass on hills, curves, at street crossings, or where there is a solid yellow line next to your lane.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check both your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if your blind spot is clear.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must have your license, registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle when driving. You must show all three when asked by police.

questions.question: The best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash is to:

options.text: Stay in the right lane on highways.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most important thing you can do to protect yourself in a crash.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, check:

options.text: Your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors to see traffic behind you. Then turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: If you see an angry driver, you should:
questions.explanation: Stay away from angry drivers. Do not make eye contact or hand gestures. Slow down, move over, or take whatever safe action you can to stay out of danger.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal three to four seconds before turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other vehicles go before you enter the intersection or roadway.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Only the alcohol effect becomes weaker.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, alcohol plus a cold medicine may affect you like having had several drinks.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

options.text: A person involved with a traffic study.

questions.explanation: You must always give the right-of-way to a blind person using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?
questions.explanation: Cold showers, black coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol level. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by:

options.text: The number of passengers in their car.

questions.explanation: Watch for aggressive drivers making wild or unsafe lane changes. Do not challenge them. The safest option is to get out of their way.

questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use their:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off the water or fog and bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: To avoid sudden stops:

options.text: Look ahead for hazards on the road.
Drive with your window partly down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead for hazards on the road.
questions.explanation: Look well ahead on the road for hazards. If you see problems early, you have time to react and do not need to stop or turn suddenly.

questions.question: If you see animals near the road while driving:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.explanation: Slow down when you see animals near the road. They may suddenly run or change direction. There may also be more animals nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Alcohol is the top cause of fatal car crashes.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is the leading killer on roadways. It affects your vision and slows your reaction time. Even small amounts of alcohol can harm your driving.

questions.question: Alcohol and drugs affect which driving skills?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills. They slow your reaction time, reduce coordination, lower alertness, and hurt concentration.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves.

questions.question: If you see a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, what should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop completely behind the gates. Wait for the tracks to clear. Then proceed when the gates rise.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely behind the gates. Wait for the tracks to clear. Then proceed when the gates rise.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when warning signs, flashing lights, or flaggers tell you a train is coming. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Move to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, you must pull to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Which of these substances can impair your driving and result in a DUI arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can affect your driving ability. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications (both prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close behind another car):

options.text: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Prevents other drivers from cutting you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous and can lead to aggressive driving. You may receive a traffic ticket for unsafe driving.

questions.question: If you just had an argument and feel angry, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play loud music so you don't think about it.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the highway to let off steam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect how safely you drive. If you are angry, upset, scared, or worried, wait until you feel calm before driving. You need to focus on the road.

questions.question: When is passing another vehicle prohibited?

options.text: Within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.
If the vehicle you're following displays a slow-moving vehicle symbol.
When using the right lane to pass a left-turning vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass any vehicle within 100 feet of a railroad crossing or intersection. Only pass when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Is smoking or preparing to smoke while driving a distraction?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving ability.
No, it helps keep drivers alert.
No, it is not a distraction.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. It creates a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming. Be ready to respond to red, yellow, or green lights.

questions.question: How can road rage and aggressive driving be reduced?
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and leave plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A blind person with a guide dog is ready to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until they cross.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until they cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until they cross the street.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes (with or without a red tip) always have the right-of-way. You must yield to them.
